instrFossabot: Open your Fossabot commands page: fossabot.com/yourchannel/commands. It is public, so there is nothing to sign in to.
Your channel name is the part of that address before /commands, normally your Twitch login.
Type that channel name below to continue.

Click “Export this dashboard to a file” and save the .json file.
Choose that file below to continue.
instrNightbot: Click “Connect Nightbot” below. You'll be sent to nightbot.tv to sign in and approve access.
Approve the request (commands, timers and spam protection, read for this import only) and you'll land right back here.
Hit Continue and pick what to import.
instrSe: Sign in at streamelements.com and open your dashboard.
Go to Account Settings → Channels, or use the direct link below.
In your browser's developer tools → Network tab, click any request to api.streamelements.com and copy the token after “Bearer ” in its Authorization header.
Paste the JWT below to continue.
instrSl: On the computer where the StreamLabs Chatbot desktop app runs, close the app first so the database is fully written.
Locate Chatbot.db and upload it below to continue.
instrWizebot: In your Wizebot panel, open the Streaming Website section and turn it on if it is off. Your command list is only published while that site is enabled.
Your channel login is the subdomain of that site: in yourchannel.streaming.lv, it is yourchannel.
Type that login below to continue.

Only commands that post chat text come over. Screen animations and sound-only commands are skipped, and when a command carries a public description, Wizebot publishes that instead of its chat message, so check the review step.

loyalty.label: Loyalty Points
loyalty.tagline: Viewers earn channel currency for subs, cheers and watch time.
loyalty.description: Give your community its own currency: viewers earn points for subscribing, resubscribing, gifting subs, cheering bits, and simply watching (everyone in chat earns on a 5-minute tick while you are live). Name the currency, tune every rate, and let mods grant points with !points set/add. Viewers check their standing with !points. Gamble and Duels spend this ledger and are armed from this page. They cannot run while the currency is off. Pairs with Counters and channel-point rewards that award points.

gamble.label: Gamble
gamble.tagline: Let viewers wager their points on a roll with !gamble.
gamble.description: Give your loyalty points a game: viewers type !gamble <amount> (or half/all of their standing) and the bot rolls 1-100. Landing inside your win chance pays the stake back plus its match; anything else takes it. Set the win odds, bet limits and per-viewer cooldown below, and customize the win/lose lines. Every payout and debit moves real loyalty points through the same ledger as !points. Turned on from the Loyalty page. It cannot run while the currency is off, and it uses the same currency name.

duel.label: Duels
duel.tagline: Viewer-vs-viewer point duels: pot free-for-alls and 1v1 challenges.
duel.description: Two ways to duel for points. A pot duel: someone types !duel <stake> and everyone has the window to add their own stake, and when time runs out the bot draws one winner weighted by stake and they take the whole pot. Or a challenge: !duel <user> <stake> names an opponent who must type !duel accept before the window closes; equal stakes, a fair coin flip, winner takes both. Decline, cancellation and no-shows always refund every escrowed point, and every movement goes through the loyalty service's guarded spend, so nobody can wager what they do not have. Turned on from the Loyalty page; it uses the same currency name and stays off while loyalty is off.

triggers.label: Trigger Words
triggers.tagline: Auto-reply when a word shows up in chat, no "!" needed.
triggers.description: Give the bot a list of words or phrases and the line to post when it sees one in ordinary chat, no command prefix required. Each rule pairs a phrase with a response: pick how the phrase matches (whole word, contains, exact message or starts with; the default matches the whole word, so "hi" will not fire inside "this"), write the reply, and switch individual rules on or off without deleting them. Responses support {user}, {random} and {choice:a,b,c}. The first matching rule wins, so one message gets at most one reply.

Fully automatic: no commands, no setup. A pyramid only counts when it is built cleanly, line by line, with nothing else posted in between.

Viewers can check their feeding rank with !bagels and the leaderboard with !bagelboard. The script is built in, nothing to configure. Switch it off to keep the bot strictly to commands.

automod.label: AutoMod
automod.tagline: Catch scams, IP-grabbers and raid spam before your mods do.
automod.description: The bot screens every chat line for harmful content and coordinated raid floods, and warns, deletes, times out or bans the sender. Trusted chatters (VIPs, mods, the broadcaster) are always exempt, and anything borderline is left to your human mods. Pick a level from None to All, then fine-tune each check below. The safety floor (hate slurs and IP-grabber links) is always enforced, on every level and even with the module off: hosting those risks your channel and the bot account platform-wide. Everything else is your call.

level.label: Enforcement level
level.help: Sets the default for every check below. The safety floor applies at every level.

harassment.label: Harassment
harassment.help: Directed harm ("kys" and friends): warns the sender and removes the message; repeat offenders are timed out, then banned.

sexual.label: Sexual content
sexual.help: Removes messages with explicit sexual terms.

profanity.label: Profanity
profanity.help: Removes plain swearing. Off by default: most channels allow it.

style.label: Caps & symbol spam
style.help: Removes shouting, symbol walls and character floods. Emote walls (KEKW spam) are recognized and never flagged.

links.label: Link-spam radar
links.help: Watches for the same link template posted by many different accounts and removes the wave. Single links are never touched.

clips_only.label: Twitch clips only
clips_only.help: Removes messages that contain any link other than a Twitch clip (clips.twitch.tv/… or twitch.tv/…/clip/…). Off by default: turn on when chat should only share clips.

block_terms.label: Blocked terms
block_terms.help: Extra words or phrases to flag in your channel. Separate with commas or new lines. Matched even through obfuscation (l33t, look-alike letters).

allow_terms.label: Allowed terms
allow_terms.help: Words that are fine in your channel: a line containing one is never flagged by the checks above or your blocked terms. Cannot override the safety floor.

shoutout.description: When another channel raids in, the bot posts a shoutout pointing your chat at the raider. Turn the module on and customize the shoutout line.

alerts.description: The bot posts a chat line when someone follows, subscribes, cheers, or raids, and can announce ad breaks. Turn each alert on or off and customize its message. New alerts default on, except the ad-break alert which stays off until you enable it. A follow alert fires at most once per viewer every three days, so unfollowing and refollowing cannot spam your chat.

queue.label: Play Queue

queue.description: Viewers type !join to get in line and !list to see who is next (the first 10). You (and your mods) run the line from chat: !queue open and !queue close accept or stop new joins, !queue next pulls up the next player, !queue remove <user> takes someone out, and !queue clear empties it. Viewers can step out any time with !leave. Turn the module on to enable the commands; the line survives closing so you can play through everyone already waiting.

raffle.label: Raffle
raffle.tagline: Timed random draws your chat enters with !join.
raffle.description: Open a raffle and viewers type !join to enter. While it runs the bot posts a time-left reminder every few minutes (the cadence is yours to set), and when time runs out it draws automatically. Winners are picked uniformly at random from everyone who entered, every entry counts once, and the draw leaves a verifiable receipt behind. Winners confirm with !claim inside a 15-minute window. You (and your mods) also control everything from chat: !raffle open starts one, !raffle draw closes early and announces, !raffle cancel tears it down without drawing. When both this and the Play Queue are on, !join belongs to the raffle and the queue is reachable through !queue join.

quotes.label: Quotes
quotes.tagline: Save the best things said on stream and replay them in chat.
quotes.description: Keep a channel quote book. Someone saves a line with !addquote the text (or !quote "the text") and the bot numbers it and stamps the save date. Anyone replays one with !quote for a random pick, !quote 12 for a specific number, or !quote ferret for a random quote containing that word. The bot answers "Quote #12: the text (2026-07-11)". Choose who is allowed to save and who may rewrite one (!quote edit 12 the fixed text) below; both default to moderators. Mods remove a mistake with !quote remove 12; numbers are never reused, so an old number keeps pointing at the same quote. The replies are fixed system text (localized to your console language).

govee.label: Govee Lights
govee.tagline: Let viewers recolour your Govee lights with channel points.
govee.description: Viewers redeem a channel-points reward, type a colour (a name like "blue" or a hex like #00ccff), and the bot turns your Govee light on and sets it. Live only: redemptions off-stream are refunded automatically. To get your Govee API key: open the Govee Home app, tap Profile (bottom right), tap the settings gear (top right), tap "Apply for API Key", fill in the short form, and Govee emails you a key within a few minutes. Then on this page: paste the key (we store it encrypted and never show it back), pick the light to control, and create the reward.

discord.tagline: One bot on Twitch and Discord. Go-live, clips, welcomes, tickets, and voice.
discord.description: Connect an existing Discord server or create one from Bagel’s template. Go-live and clips post from outgress directly. They never wait on sesame. Raids, gift bombs, and milestone subs copy into #announcements when you turn those on. The Discord gateway (dingress) handles welcomes, join-to-create voice, support tickets, staff logs, slash moderation, and crumb ranks.

songqueue.label: Song Requests
songqueue.tagline: !sr and a channel-points reward that queue songs from Spotify.
songqueue.description: Register your own Spotify app and connect your account to it once, then let viewers queue music two ways: the !sr chat command (with a permission tier you pick, from everyone down to just you) and a channel-points reward whose typed input is the song query: a name, "artist - song", or a pasted Spotify link. The bot announces what is playing, resolves links and search names against Spotify, and keeps one song per viewer in the up-next list. !current reads your Spotify player directly, so it answers even for tracks nobody requested. Moderators manage the queue with !sr next, remove and clear.

touser.name: Named person
touser.hint: first argument, e.g. a mentioned user
touser.desc: The first word typed after the command ("@" removed); the viewer themself when blank. {target} works too.

args.name: Everything typed after
args.desc: All text after the command, as one string.

positional.name: Word number
positional.hint: word 1 typed after the command; {2} is the next one, up to {30}; {2:4} takes a range
positional.desc: Word 1 typed after the command. {2} is the next one, and so on up to {30}. Empty when that word was not typed. {2:} takes a word through to the end, as one string; change the number to start elsewhere, {1:} is the whole thing. {2:4} takes words 2 through 4 the same way, and {:2} is the same range starting at word 1 (the first two words). Naming an end past the last word actually typed just stops at that last word; naming the end before the start, like {4:2}, is left exactly as written.
positional.restHint: word 2 through to the end, as one string
positional.leadingHint: the first 2 words, as one string

channel.name: Channel name
channel.hint: the channel the command runs in

userid.name: Viewer ID
userid.hint: the Twitch user ID of whoever ran the command
userid.desc: The viewer's Twitch user ID. It never changes, even after a rename.

userLogin.name: Viewer login
userLogin.hint: their lowercase login, not their display name
userLogin.desc: Their lowercase login, which can differ from the display name {user} shows.

command.name: Command name
command.hint: the command’s own name, without the “!”
command.desc: The name of the command that ran, without the "!". Alternate names all report the main one.

counter.name: Counter
counter.hint: shows a counter's current value; {count:…} is the same read (Loyalty)
counter.desc: Shows a counter's current value without changing it. To add to a counter, turn on "Bump a counter" on the command itself; this only reads whatever that option (or !counter) has produced. {counter:target:name} reads the mentioned viewer's own count instead of the channel's. Needs the Loyalty Points module.
counter.targetHint: the mentioned viewer's own count, not the channel's

random.name: Random 1-100
random.hint: a random number from 1 to 100, or {random:min-max}
random.desc: A whole number from 1 to 100, new every time. {random:1-6} picks your own range; both ends included.
random.rangeHint: a random number in your own range

choice.name: Random choice
choice.hint: picks one of the comma-separated options at random
choice.desc: Picks one of your comma-separated options. Replace the words.

math.name: Arithmetic
math.hint: evaluates a small sum: + - * / and parentheses
math.desc: Works out a small sum. Whole numbers, + - * / and parentheses; nothing else.

querystring.name: Arguments, URL-encoded
querystring.hint: everything typed after the command, URL-encoded for a data source
querystring.desc: Everything typed after the command, encoded so it can be dropped into a data source URL.

queryescape.name: URL-encode text
queryescape.hint: URL-encodes the text you put after the colon
queryescape.desc: Encodes your own text for the query part of a URL. Replace the words.

pathescape.name: URL-encode a path
pathescape.hint: URL-encodes the text for a path, not a query
pathescape.desc: The same, for the path part of a URL, where a space is not a plus.

repeat.name: Repeat a phrase
repeat.hint: repeats a phrase n times (up to 20, one chat line)
repeat.desc: Repeats your phrase, space separated. Up to 20 times, and it has to fit one chat line.

countdown.name: Time until a date
countdown.hint: how long until that date (YYYY-MM-DD, or a full timestamp)
countdown.desc: How long until that date. Write it as YYYY-MM-DD, or as a full timestamp. Nothing once the date has passed.

countup.name: Time since a date
countup.desc: How long since that date, in the same wording as !uptime.

if.name: Say one thing or another
if.hint: one text or another: {if:name:when it has something:when it does not}, or {if:name=value:…:…} for an exact match. Variables do not work inside the two texts
if.desc: Picks the first text when the variable you name has something in it, the second when it does not. Name it without braces, and write {if:game=Chess:…:…} to test an exact value instead. Variables do not work inside the two texts. Leave the second one out and a false test says nothing at all, if that empties the whole line, the bot skips that line rather than sending a blank message.

followage.name: Time following
followage.hint: how long they have followed the channel (Followage module)
followage.desc: How long the viewer has followed you, in the same wording as !followage. {followage:alex} asks about someone else, and someone who does not follow comes back empty. Needs the Followage module.

accountage.name: Account age
accountage.hint: how old their Twitch account is (Account age module)
accountage.desc: How old their Twitch account is. {accountage:alex} asks about someone else. Needs the Account age module.

points.name: Points balance
points.hint: their points balance, or {points:login} for someone else (Loyalty)
points.desc: What the viewer has earned. {points:alex} shows someone else, as long as this channel has seen them speak. Reading only: it never grants. Needs the Loyalty Points module.

pointsname.name: Name of your points
pointsname.hint: your channel’s name for its points (Loyalty)
pointsname.desc: Whatever you called your points in the Loyalty Points module, so one reply reads right on every channel.

watchtime.name: Time watched
watchtime.hint: how long they have watched, in the same words as !uptime (Loyalty)
watchtime.desc: How long they have watched while the loyalty clock was running. {watchtime:alex} asks about someone else. Needs the Loyalty Points module.

uses.name: Times used
uses.hint: how many times this command has been used, not counting this one; {uses} is the same thing (approximate)
uses.desc: How many times this command has been used in your channel, not counting the one printing it. It counts every use, whichever name was typed, and needs no counter. {uses} is the older spelling of the same value. The total is approximate: the bot batches its counting, so it can be up to a minute behind.

quote.name: A saved quote
quote.hint: a random saved quote, or {quote:12} for a numbered one (Quotes module)
quote.desc: A random quote from your quote book, worded exactly as !quote says it. {quote:12} picks a numbered one, and a number nobody has used comes back empty. Two {quote} in one response are two different quotes. Needs the Quotes module.

time.name: Your local time
time.hint: your local time, on the clock face you set (Local time module); {time:Paris} for anywhere else, no module needed
time.desc: The time where you are, on the timezone and clock face you set on the Local time module. Needs that module, with a timezone saved. {time:Paris} looks up a different place instead — a city, a country, an abbreviation like EST or a UTC offset — and works even without the module: it just needs no timezone of its own, only the clock face you picked if you ever set one. A place it does not recognize comes back empty.
time.placeHint: the time at a place you name, no module needed

song.name: Now playing
song.hint: the track playing right now, or {song.title} / {song.artist} (Song requests)
song.desc: The track playing on Spotify right now. {song.title} and {song.artist} give the two halves separately. Nothing playing comes back empty. Needs the Song requests module.

chatters.name: People in chat
chatters.hint: how many people have talked in chat recently
chatters.desc: How many people have talked in chat recently. It counts chatters the bot has seen speak, not everyone with the page open, and a quiet channel comes back as 0.

randomChatter.name: A random chatter
randomChatter.hint: one of them, picked at random (never you, never the bot)
randomChatter.desc: The name of one person who has talked recently, picked at random. Never you and never the bot. Two of them in one response are two separate picks, and a silent channel comes back empty.

randomViewer.name: A random viewer
randomViewer.hint: someone in chat right now, picked at random (never you, never the bot)
randomViewer.desc: The name of one person Twitch says is in chat right now, picked at random — not someone who has necessarily said anything. Never you and never the bot. Two of them in one response are two separate picks. Right after the bot restarts, before it has loaded who is in chat, it names someone who has spoken recently instead.

emotes.name: Emote list
emotes.hint: every global emote code from one provider — {emotes:7tv}, {emotes:bttv} or {emotes:ffz} — space-separated
emotes.desc: The global emote codes for one provider (7TV, BetterTTV or FrankerFaceZ), separated by spaces. These are the ones every channel has, not the emotes you added to yours, and a long list is cut to fit one chat line.

randomEmote.name: A random emote
randomEmote.hint: one emote code picked at random from those global sets
randomEmote.desc: One emote code drawn at random from those lists. Two of them in one response are two separate picks. If the bot has not loaded any codes yet, it comes back empty.

uptime.name: Stream uptime
uptime.hint: how long you have been live, empty when you are offline (!uptime toggle)
uptime.desc: How long the stream has been live, worded the way !uptime words it. Offline comes back empty, so give it a default. {uptime:someone} does the same for another channel. Follows the !uptime toggle.

title.name: Stream title
title.hint: your current stream title, or {title:someone} for another channel (!title toggle)
title.desc: The current stream title, the same one !title shows. It works offline too. {title:someone} gives another channel’s. Follows the !title toggle.

game.name: Stream category
game.hint: the category you are streaming, or {game:someone} for another channel (!game toggle)
game.desc: The category being streamed, the same one !game shows. It works offline too. {game:someone} gives another channel’s, which is what a shoutout command wants. Follows the !game toggle.

channelViewers.name: Viewers watching
channelViewers.hint: how many people are watching right now, 0 when you are offline
channelViewers.desc: How many people are watching right now, straight from Twitch. An offline channel comes back as 0. Bare {channel} stays your channel name.

followers.name: Follower count
followers.desc: Your current follower count, straight from Twitch. Takes no payload — it always counts your own channel.

subs.name: Subscriber count
subs.desc: Your current subscriber count, straight from Twitch. Takes no payload — it always counts your own channel.

urlfetch.name: Fetched value
urlfetch.hint: Insert a fetched value from a saved API definition
urlfetch.desc: One value from a saved data source definition (Data sources page). Write {urlfetch:name} for the whole response, or add a dot path to reach one field inside a JSON response, such as {urlfetch:weather.forecast.current.temp_f}.

songTitle.name: Song title
songTitle.hint: just the track title, the first half of {song}
songTitle.desc: The track title on its own, the first half of {song}. Nothing playing comes back empty. Needs the Song requests module.

songArtist.name: Song artist
songArtist.hint: just the artist name, the second half of {song}
songArtist.desc: The artist name on its own, the second half of {song}. Nothing playing comes back empty. Needs the Song requests module.

raider.name: Raider name
raider.hint: Friendly display name of the raiding channel
raider.desc: Friendly display name of the raiding channel.

time.name: Local time
time.desc: The clock, in your configured timezone and format.

time.name: Local time
time.hint: The clock at the looked-up place
time.desc: The clock, at the place a viewer asked about.

date.name: Local date
date.hint: Today's date at the looked-up place
date.desc: Today's date, at the place a viewer asked about.

place.name: Place
place.hint: The place a viewer asked about
place.desc: The normalized place name the lookup resolved.

timezone.name: Timezone
timezone.desc: The timezone name or offset at the looked-up place.

count.name: Still waiting
count.hint: How many people remain in line
count.desc: How many people remain in line.

user.name: Invoker
user.hint: The mod who pulled up the next player

fkdr.name: FKDR
fkdr.hint: Final kills divided by final deaths
fkdr.desc: Final kills divided by final deaths.

draws.name: Draws
draws.hint: Season matches that ended with no winner
draws.desc: Season matches that ended with no winner.

draws.name: Draws
draws.hint: Matches this stream that ended with no winner
draws.desc: Matches this stream that ended with no winner.

firststructure.name: First structure avg
firststructure.hint: Average split for whichever structure was entered first
firststructure.desc: Average split for whichever structure was entered first.

secondstructure.name: Second structure avg
secondstructure.hint: Average split for whichever structure was entered second
secondstructure.desc: Average split for whichever structure was entered second.

opponent.name: Opponent
opponent.hint: The other player in that match
opponent.desc: The other player in that match.

result.name: Result
result.desc: Win, loss or draw. Forfeits and decay matches are called out too.

time.name: Time
time.desc: The match's completion time, when it reached one.

seed.name: Seed
seed.hint: The seed type for that match
seed.desc: The seed type for that match.

structure.name: Structure
structure.hint: The bastion structure type for that match
structure.desc: The bastion structure type for that match.

ago.name: Ago
ago.hint: How long ago that match ended
ago.desc: How long ago that match ended.

playera.name: Player A
playera.desc: The first typed player (or you, with one name typed).

winsa.name: Wins A
winsa.hint: Player A's wins over player B
winsa.desc: Player A's wins over player B.

winsb.name: Wins B
winsb.hint: Player B's wins over player A
winsb.desc: Player B's wins over player A.

list.name: Top 5
list.desc: The top 5 rows, pre-formatted as one line.

time.name: Time
time.hint: The player's own time this week
time.desc: The player's own time this week, when they have one.

time.name: Time
time.hint: The personal best for the requested window
time.desc: The personal best for the requested window.

window.name: Window
window.desc: Which window answered: daily, weekly, monthly, all-time or ranked.

window.name: Window
window.hint: Which stats window: lifetime or season
window.desc: Which stats window: lifetime or season.

count.name: Item count
count.hint: How many items are in the shop
count.desc: How many items are in the shop.

user.name: Chatter
user.hint: The person whose message matched the rule
user.desc: The person whose message matched the rule.

input.name: Viewer input
input.desc: The text typed with the redemption (when the reward asks for one).

reward.name: Reward title
reward.hint: The name of the redeemed reward
reward.desc: The name of the redeemed reward.

counter.name: Bound counter
counter.desc: The bound counter's new value, when the reward has one. Give it command scope for one pooled total shared by every redemption of this reward.

points.name: Loyalty points
points.hint: Loyalty points the reward grants (when positive)
points.desc: Loyalty points the reward grants (when positive).

input.name: Viewer input
input.hint: The colour text the viewer typed
input.desc: The colour text the viewer typed with the redemption.

color.name: Colour
color.desc: The colour name the bot matched and set the lights to.

input.name: Viewer input
input.hint: The song text the viewer typed
input.desc: The song name, "artist - song", or link the viewer typed with the redemption.

pos.name: Queue position
pos.hint: The track's position in the queue
pos.desc: The track's position in the queue.

validation.commandNameMax: Command name must be at most {max} characters.
validation.commandNameBang: Command name only carries the "!" in chat. Leave it out here.
validation.alternateNameMax: Alternate name "{name}" must be at most {max} characters.
validation.alternateNameBang: Alternate name "{name}" only carries the "!" in chat. Leave it out here.
validation.aliasOwnName: "{name}" is already the command's own name.
validation.responseLinesMax: Response can be at most {max} lines. Each line is sent as its own chat message.
validation.responseCharsMax: Each line must be at most {max} characters.
validation.responseFetchMax: A response can reference at most {max} different fetched values ({urlfetch:…}).
validation.cooldownRange: Cooldown must be between 0 and {max} seconds.
validation.cooldownInteger: Cooldown must be a whole number of seconds.
validation.userIdNumeric: User restriction must be a numeric Twitch user id.
validation.definitionNameMax: Definition name must be at most {max} characters.
validation.definitionNameCharset: Use lower-case letters, digits and underscores only.
validation.urlMax: URL must be at most {max} characters.
validation.urlPublic: URL must point at a public https host.
validation.plainPath: A plain fetch reads the whole body. Clear the path or switch to json.
validation.pathDepth: Path can be at most {max} segments deep.
validation.pathSegment: "{segment}" cannot be used as a path segment: letters, digits, "-" and "_" only.
validation.keyLabelMax: Key label must be at most {max} characters.
validation.fetchExists: A data source named "{name}" already exists.
validation.fetchLimit: At most {max} data sources per channel.
